title: Reading the comments: An exploratory quantitative analysis of YouTube comments in response to abortion plotlines on fictional television programs
screen_reason: Quantitative content analysis of 619 abortion-relevant YouTube comments under 15 official-network clips of US television abortion plotlines. Comments were double-coded with an a priori codebook including 'potential misinformation about abortion or abortion policy... defined as factually inaccurate medical or political content about abortion'; 10.4% (n = 64) carried that code. That is a share of items judged inaccurate against a stated factual standard, so CONTENT.

estimates.country: United States (clips of U.S. television abortion plotlines on official U.S. network YouTube channels; commenters' own country not recorded)
estimates.date: Clips posted 2018-2023 (sample period); comment download date not reported
estimates.measure_type: % of abortion-relevant YouTube comments containing potential misinformation about abortion or abortion policy
estimates.denominator: 619 comments coded as relevant (pertaining to abortion) from the top 20 comments plus all their replies under the 15 clips that had more than 10 relevant comments; 2,426 comments in total were coded across 25 clips
estimates.definition: Comment carried the code 'potential misinformation about abortion or abortion policy', i.e. factually inaccurate medical or political content about abortion (examples given: abortion leading to infertility; abortion being illegal in every U.S. state)
estimates.misinfo_def: "Emergent codes included potential misinformation about abortion or abortion policy which we defined as factually inaccurate medical or political content about abortion, such as abortion leading to infertility, or abortion being illegal in every U.S. state."
estimates.source_quote: The only other content category present in greater than 10 % of comments was potential misinformation about abortion (10.4 %, n = 64)
estimates.page_loc: p. 4, Results 'Content'; Table 3 (Claims about abortion: Potential misinformation 64, 10.4); Abstract
estimates.ground_truth_detail: A priori codebook developed by the research team, piloted on two clips; all clips and comments double-coded by two research assistants who watched the clip first, differences adjudicated with a senior RA and, failing consensus, a senior author; coders consulted the first or last author when unsure whether a comment contained misinformation; percent agreement for the final coding round ranged 74%-100% across coding categories (no kappa reported)
estimates.moderator_quote: Given the high volume of comments, for feasibility purposes, we elected to code the top 20 comments and associated replies to these comments. This approach is consistent with other scholarship analyzing YouTube comments, represents the comments that are most likely to be seen by most viewers, and are also most popular with viewers, as they have been voted "up".
estimates.notes: Denominator judgement: the paper's own base is the 619 abortion-RELEVANT comments, so 10.4% is the share of on-topic comments, not of all comments in these threads. Using the verbatim total of 2,426 coded comments, the all-comment share would be 64/2,426 = 2.6%; not made a row because the misinformation code applies only to abortion-relevant content and the paper never presents that base. Sample is doubly curated: only clips on official network channels (25 clips = 9% of the 275 abortion plotlines in the period), and only the top 20 (most-liked) comments plus replies, then only the 15 clips with >10 relevant comments. year coded 2025 (publication year) because the comment-scrape date is nowhere reported - the article cites a June 2025 Nielsen report, so the scrape is 2024-2025, while the clips themselves date from 2018-2023. The code name is 'POTENTIAL misinformation', a deliberate hedge by the authors, though the definition is a factual-accuracy standard.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Sentiment shares (abortion positive 43.8%, restrictive 22.0%, complex 18.7%) are attitude codes, not veracity, so no rows. (2) 'Abortion is murder' (8.4%), 'religion as related to abortion' (8.2%), 'storyline is unrealistic' (2.8%) are opinion or plotline-commentary codes, not factual-accuracy judgements. (3) The by-sentiment breakdown of misinformation comments (of misinformation comments expressing sentiment: 65.6% n=42 restrictive, 21.8% n=12 positive, 10.9% n=6 complex) is a subgroup of the extracted row and its base (misinformation comments that expressed any sentiment, n=64 minus those with no sentiment) is not the paper's headline, so it was collapsed away. (4) Relevance rates per clip (0 to 49.0%, median 22.6%) describe topicality, not misinformation. (5) Exposure figures exist for videos (average 547,948 views, range 3,057-2.3m) but comments are never weighted by views or likes, so no EXPOSURE row is possible. (6) No CONCENTRATION statistic (e.g. share of misinformation comments from a few accounts) is reported. (7) Introduction statistics quoted from Nielsen/Pew (YouTube 12% of US television viewing; 83% of adults, 93% of teens ever use YouTube) are cited from elsewhere and excluded per R8.

rob.design: Exploratory cross-sectional content analysis. Purposive frame: from 275 abortion plotlines aired 2018-2023, two RAs searched YouTube by show/episode/'abortion' terms and kept only clips posted on official network channels, yielding 25 clips from 21 plotlines (9% of possible plotlines); comments downloaded via the YouTube API, sorted by 'top comments' (most liked), and only the top 20 plus their replies coded per clip (2,426 comments, mean 97 per video); analysis restricted to the 15 clips with >10 abortion-relevant comments, giving 619 relevant comments of which 82.7% were replies. All comments double-coded against an a priori, pilot-tested codebook with adjudication by a senior RA and senior authors; percent agreement 74%-100% across categories, no kappa; comment quotes modified to prevent user identification. Not a random or complete sample of comments, clips, or commenters, and commenter demographics/geography are unknown.
rob.item6_quote: Emergent codes included potential misinformation about abortion or abortion policy which we defined as factually inaccurate medical or political content about abortion, such as abortion leading to infertility, or abortion being illegal in every U.S. state.
rob.item10_quote: The only other content category present in greater than 10 % of comments was potential misinformation about abortion (10.4 %, n = 64)
